title: TransactionCertificate
description: Evidence for one multi-agent transaction, issued whether it committed or was refused. Refusals need this more than commits: a commit leaves a trace in the network, a refusal leaves nothing behind unless something records it, and the refusal is what an operator is later asked to justify.

refusals.description: Every reason the transaction was refused, prefixed by the stage that refused it (telemetry., identity., authority., per_action_blocked:, aggregate.). A refusal certificate carrying no reasons is not evidence.

telemetry_checks.description: The trust gate's verdict, per check. Present for passes as well as failures.

authorized.description: null when the transaction was refused before authority ran — an identity or telemetry refusal. The record still names the agent that tried.

aggregate_checks.description: Every aggregate invariant evaluated, satisfied or not. Recording the passes is what distinguishes 'this limit was checked and held' from 'this limit was never checked'.

priority.description: The operator-programmed priority that decided this, read from the authority policy and never from the envelope.

dropped.description: Requests conflict resolution declined to apply. Resolution drops requests rather than rewriting values, so a dropped member means that dimension keeps whatever the network already had.

admitted.description: Referenced by digest rather than inlined: the per-action SafetyCertificate is the authoritative record of each emission, and duplicating it here would create two things that can disagree.

signature.description: Hex Ed25519 over the canonical bytes, constructed exactly as horizon_ric.shield.signing.canonical_certificate_bytes does — sorted keys, compact separators, signature fields removed. A verifier written for one works for the other.

baseline_digest.description: SHA-256 of the network state the bundle was decided against. Without it a refusal certificate cannot be replayed: the same bundle against a different baseline decides differently.

aggregates.description: The aggregate limits that were configured, with their thresholds. Naming the violated invariant is not enough — the same invariant with a different floor decides differently.

epoch.description: The cycle this transaction closed, or -1 when evaluated outside a cycle.

margin.description: null where the underlying margin was infinite. json.dumps emits a bare Infinity, which is not valid JSON, and signed bytes a conforming parser cannot read are not evidence.
